policy: Ten independent console ports. Metadata and CI validation never imply hardware compatibility. Source builds, kernel boot, userspace, graphics and physical hardware are separate evidence gates. CI performs host-side source builds only; no firmware modification, exploit execution, payload deployment or physical-console writes.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation Portable
targets.toolchain_strategy: MIPS little-endian cross-toolchain; ABI and kernel config audit
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: Historical Linux feasibility research; no Snakey kernel, boot chain or usable desktop is established.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation Vita
targets.toolchain_strategy: ARM hard-float cross-toolchain; pinned upstream Vita build adapter
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: A pinned Vita Linux Next upstream build exists in CI; this is not a Snakey kernel or a hardware boot.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation 3
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and shell feasibility first; XFCE is not assumed
targets.notes: PS3-specific Linux support exists in upstream kernel history; OtherOS availability and usable memory are model/configuration dependent.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation 4
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: First integration target. Linux psX source and limited model-specific evidence; no Snakey kernel build or console boot is claimed.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation 5
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: Separate PS5 patch ecosystem; exact kernel base, model and firmware compatibility require source audit.

targets.name: Microsoft Xbox Original
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and shell feasibility first; XFCE is not assumed
targets.notes: Historical Xbox Linux projects exist; legacy boot and graphics support require independent audit.

targets.name: Nintendo Wii
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and shell feasibility first; XFCE is not assumed
targets.notes: Historical Wii Linux work; severe memory constraints make a conventional desktop unlikely.

targets.name: Nintendo Wii U
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: Independent platform port required; do not reuse Wii kernel assumptions.

targets.name: Nintendo Switch
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: Community Linux ecosystem exists; device tree, GPU, display, input and network support must be audited.

targets.name: Nintendo Switch 2
targets.cpu: NVIDIA custom ARM SoC (exact Linux enablement audit required)
targets.desktop_goal: Kernel and minimal userspace first; graphical session only after display/input/GPU driver validation
targets.notes: Research lane only. No verified Snakey upstream source, kernel build or Linux boot claim.
